identities.label: Hindu Shahis
identities.description: former dynasty in Pakistan and Afghanistan
identities.summary:
The Hindu Shahis, also referred to as the Kabul Shahis and Odi Shahis, were a dynasty that ruled Kabulistan, Gandhara and Punjab between 822 CE and 1026 CE, succeeding the Turk Shahis.
The dynasty was founded by Kalarapāla in c. 822 CE after overthrowing Lagaturman, the last Turk Shahi king. His successor Samantadeva lost the region of Kabul to the Saffarid dynasty, but Lalliya soon re-conquered Kabul and subdued the region of Zabulistan as well. He also fought against the Utpala dynasty.
